titleTr: Okuma stratejileri: ana fikir, çıkarım, bağlamdan tahmin

grammar.topic: Reading strategies: main idea, inference, vocabulary in context
explainTr: Sınav okumasında önce soruları oku, sonra metne geç. Böylece neyi aradığını bilirsin. Skimming (hızlı göz gezdirme) genel fikri verir; scanning (arama okuması) tarih, isim, sayı gibi belirli bilgiyi bulur.

Ana fikir çoğunlukla paragrafın ilk cümlesindedir; son cümle onu tekrarlayabilir. Çıkarım (inference) sorusunda cevap açıkça yazmaz; metindeki ipuçlarından en mantıklı sonucu seçersin. Bilinmeyen kelimede durma: önceki ve sonraki cümleye, ön eke/son eke bak.

Seçenekleri elerken metinde olmayanı, aşırıyı (always, never, only) ve konudan sapanı çıkar. İki seçenek kalırsa metne dön ve kanıt ara. Emin olamadığın soruyu boş bırakma: eleme yap ve en makul olanı işaretle.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'Ana fikir nedir?' sorusuna kendi cümlenle cevap verirsin; sınavda ise hazır seçenekler arasından metne en uygun olanı bulursun. Bu yüzden kelimesi kelimesine benzeyen seçenek değil, anlamı en iyi özetleyen seçenek doğrudur.
table: he looked at his watch → impatient
çevre cümleye ve kelime köküne bak
yanlış, aşırı, konu dışı seçeneği çıkar

exercises.q: Which sentence usually states the main idea of a paragraph?
options: The topic sentence, often the first one
exercises.whyTr: Ana fikir çoğunlukla ilk cümlede (topic sentence) bulunur.

exercises.q:
Mr. Brown checked his watch for the third time. He tapped his fingers on the desk and looked toward the door.

What can you infer?
options: He is angry at his watch
He has just started his job
exercises.whyTr: Saate bakma, parmak vurma ve kapıya bakma sabırsızlık ipucudur.

exercises.q:
The substitute was reluctant to speak in front of the whole school, so she asked a colleague to introduce her.

What does "reluctant" most likely mean?
exercises.whyTr: Bağlam: başkasından tanıtmasını istedi, yani konuşmak istemedi.

exercises.q:
Many schools now offer after-school clubs. Chess club helps students think strategically. Art club builds creativity. Even a simple reading club can make shy students more confident.

What is the main idea?
options: After-school clubs help students in different ways
Art is more important than reading
exercises.whyTr: Tüm cümleler kulüplerin farklı faydalarını anlatır.

exercises.q: By the time the bell rang, Hafsa ___ the whole lesson.
exercises.whyTr: Zilden önce biten iş: past perfect.

exercises.q: If the sub plan ___ unclear, ask the office.
The answer ___ in the second paragraph.
The writer thinks schools ___ start later in the morning.
exercises.whyTr: Görüş/tavsiye: should + yalın fiil (ought to olmalıydı).

exercises.answer: The author's attitude toward homework is negative

exercises.q: To find a specific date quickly in a long text, you should ___.
exercises.whyTr: Belirli bilgi için scanning (göz gezdirme) yapılır.

exercises.q: Look at the words around an unknown word to guess its meaning from the ___.
exercises.whyTr: Bilinmeyen kelime çevresindeki ipuçlarıyla (context) tahmin edilir.

reading.title: The quiet power of substitute teachers
reading.text:
Every day in the United States, thousands of classrooms are led by substitute teachers. Many people assume that a substitute only babysits students until the regular teacher returns. However, research suggests that the quality of a substitute's day can have a significant effect on learning.

According to a recent district report, students who have a well-prepared substitute lose far less learning time than students whose substitute feels lost. The report does not blame the substitutes. Instead, it points out that the best days happen when three things come together: clear sub plans, helpful colleagues, and a substitute who is willing to ask questions.

Take the example of a sixth-grade class in Ohio. When their teacher was sick, a substitute named Mr. Ortiz arrived twenty minutes early. He read the plan, introduced himself to the teacher next door, and wrote the schedule on the board. He also put a small box of pencils and extra paper on the desk, just in case. By nine o'clock, the students knew exactly what to expect. At the end of the day, he left a detailed note describing what each group had finished. The regular teacher later said that she could continue the lesson the next morning without losing a single day.

Of course, the job is not always easy. Substitutes often enter unfamiliar rooms, meet students who test their patience, and must adapt quickly. Some districts now offer short training courses and mentors to new substitutes. Those programs, the report concludes, are cheap compared with the benefits. Schools that invest in them see fewer discipline problems and happier staff.

Ultimately, the report invites readers to change their perspective. A substitute is not an emergency solution; he or she is a member of the school team. When schools treat substitutes as professionals, substitutes respond with professional work, and students are the ones who gain the most.

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Substitutes can make a real difference when schools support them
Students learn nothing on substitute days
questions.whyTr: Metin boyunca destekli vekil öğretmenin öğrenmeyi koruduğu anlatılır.

questions.q: In the first paragraph, "assume" most likely means ___.
questions.whyTr: Bağlam: 'Many people assume ... only babysits' = kontrol etmeden sanmak.

questions.q: Why does the writer mention Mr. Ortiz?
options: To explain how to become a substitute
To show how preparation helps learning
questions.whyTr: Ortiz örneği hazırlıklı vekilin faydasını gösterir.

questions.q: What is the writer's attitude toward substitutes?
questions.whyTr: Son paragraf: 'a member of the school team ... professionals'.

script.speaker: Emre
script.text: Mom, try this practice passage. First, read the questions before you read the text.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Before the text? That feels strange.

script.speaker: Emre
script.text: It helps. Then you know what to look for.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: What if I meet a word I don't know?

script.speaker: Emre
script.text: Don't stop. Look at the sentence around it. If the text says, "She was reluctant to talk, so she stayed silent," what does reluctant mean?

script.speaker: Emre
script.text: Exactly! For the main idea, look at the first sentence of each paragraph. The last sentence often repeats it.

script.speaker: Emre
script.text: The answer isn't written directly. The text gives clues, and you choose the most logical idea.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I will practice every day this week.

script.speaker: Emre
script.text: One more tip. On test day, if you can't decide, cross out the options that are clearly wrong.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Thank you, Emre. I feel much more ready now.

writing.promptTr: Test gününden önce kendine bir mektup yaz (120-180 kelime): 16 haftada neler öğrendin, hangi konular sana zor geldi ve sınav gününde hangi stratejileri kullanacaksın? Farklı zamanları ve modalleri kullan.
writing.promptEn: Write a letter to yourself before the test (120-180 words). Say what you have learned in sixteen weeks, what was difficult, and which strategies you will use on test day.
frames: In the last sixteen weeks, I have ...
When I started, I couldn't ... but now I can ...
If I feel nervous, I should ...
writing.model:
Dear Hafsa,

In the last sixteen weeks, you have learned more than you expected. When you started, you couldn't read a school email without a dictionary, but now you can understand most of it. You have studied tenses, conditionals, the passive, reported speech, and modal verbs, and you have also learned many new words for school and work.

The most difficult topic was probably conditionals, because Turkish does not use the same pattern. If you had not practiced every day, you would not have improved so much.

On test day, you will read the questions first, and then you will look for the main idea in each paragraph. If you meet a new word, you should guess the meaning from the context. If you feel nervous, take a deep breath. You must not panic, and you don't have to answer every question perfectly.

Remember your goal: one day you will stand in front of a class as a teacher. This test is only one step. Good luck!

With love,
Hafsa
checklistTr: Present perfect (have learned) ve past simple'ı doğru kullandın mı?
En az bir koşul cümlen ve bir modal (should, must, don't have to) var mı?
Test stratejilerinden en az ikisini yazdın mı?

examSet.whyTr: For + süre, hâlâ süren çalışma: present perfect.

examSet.q: She realized she ___ the answer sheet at home.
examSet.whyTr: Fark etmeden önce olan iş: past perfect.

examSet.q: I promise I ___ you as soon as I get the results.
If I ___ the sub plan, I would have known what to do.
I wish I ___ more time to prepare for the test.
The results ___ by email next week.
"Where is the exam room?" she asked. → She asked where the exam room ___.
examSet.whyTr: Soru aktarımında düz sıra ve geçmişe kayma: was.

examSet.q: He ___ be at school; his car isn't in the lot.

When the name "Hafsa Odabasi" was called, she stood up slowly. Her hands were shaking, but she took a deep breath and smiled.

How did she feel?
examSet.whyTr: Titreyen eller = gergin; derin nefes ve gülümseme = kararlı.

examSet.q:
The note on the door said, "Back in ten minutes." Forty minutes later, the door was still locked, and a line of parents had formed in the hallway.

What can you infer?
options: The office closed for the year
The person was away longer than promised
The note was written by parents
examSet.whyTr: Not on dakika dedi ama kırk dakika sonra hâlâ kilitli.

examSet.q:
Reading the questions first saves time because it tells you what to look for. Skimming shows the general idea, and scanning finds specific details. Good readers use both.

What is the main idea?
options: Using different reading strategies helps readers work better
examSet.whyTr: Metin farklı okuma stratejilerinin birlikte kullanılmasını anlatır.
